definition: Navigating using visual input alone — embodied agents that map, localize, and plan from pixels.
details: Navigating using visual input alone — embodied agents that map, localize, and plan from pixels.

explainer.lead: Visual navigation is navigating using visual input alone, by embodied agents that map, localize and plan from pixels. It matters because it ties perception directly to movement without other sensing.

tiers.eli5: Getting around using only what you can see—like finding your way through a room by looking, with no map handed to you.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners build embodied agents that map, localize and plan from pixels. A pitfall is that relying on visual input alone makes the agent dependent on what the camera actually captures.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as navigating using visual input alone, with embodied agents that map, localize, and plan from pixels.

explainer.example: An embodied agent receives only pixel input and uses it to map its surroundings, localize itself, and plan a route.
